answer-577540502.title: I want to do acoustics research and publish, but I only have general physics and my school has no acoustics lab. Where do I start?
answer-577540502.summary: Without a lab, the obvious route is numerical acoustic simulation, validated against analytical solutions. That takes strong math.

answer-567280674.title: Just how bad can someone be at drawing?
answer-567280674.summary: At the Miffy Museum in the Netherlands, a parade of Miffy as visitors from all over the world picture her: blue, green, long-faced and melancholy, evolved into a cat…

answer-564976270.summary: That toilets are for squatting, you bring your own paper, and you air-dry your hands. My German colleague came out of his first public toilet limping.

answer-564807572.title: They say the south eats rice and the north eats noodles. How extreme are China’s regional food differences?
answer-564807572.summary: When a classmate from the south first came to Northeast China for university, she and her mom ordered four dishes, ignoring the restaurant owner’s warnings.

answer-564455232.title: Which Chinese universities are strongest in automotive NVH?
answer-564455232.summary: A list of Chinese universities with strong vehicle engineering and NVH groups, from Tsinghua, SJTU and Tongji to Jilin, Hunan and South China University of Technology.

zhihu-53679019.title: PhD diary, part 1: Wednesday, February 12, 2014, sunny

Foreword: I started a PhD in Germany in 2013 and graduated in 2018, and all through it I kept a diary written only for myself. Now, through those diaries, I look back on the 1,800-plus days of my PhD, my days before thirty, and hold a time-traveling conversation with myself. Let five years of growing up serve as a warning to the world: be kind to every lovable, long-suffering PhD student. I love the big floor-to-ceiling window in my new office: look up and you can see blue sky and white clouds…

answer-522738406.summary: It reminded me of “Youth,” the song from Reply 1988. Swap first love and youth for Rose’s career, and it couldn’t fit better.

answer-514306872.title: What classic or fun papers have you come across in your field?

answer-510079266.title: What do you make of Jia Zhangke’s film Ash Is Purest White?
answer-510079266.summary: My first Jia Zhangke film took me straight back to 2001: small-town gangsters, the Shanxi I pictured as a child, a China racing ahead, and Zhao Tao’s explosive performance.

answer-505286467.title: My train reaches Harbin East at 5:50 a.m. and my flight leaves at 9:40. Can I make it, and what’s the fastest way to the airport?
answer-505286467.summary: A taxi should take less than an hour.

answer-504515893.title: Which music genre do you hate most, and why?
answer-504515893.summary: Harsh vocals. One song and my temples are ready to explode.

answer-504515276.summary: Whether they’d be good-looking is hard to say, but over 95% of the half-European, half-East Asian people I know show no visible trace of European genes.

answer-504513481.title: What’s the most physically painful thing you’ve ever experienced?
answer-504513481.summary: Taking a football to the cr*tch in high school, in full view of the girls’ cheering squad, and pretending it hit my stomach.

answer-504509168.title: What did your college roommates do that utterly disgusted you?
answer-504509168.summary: Our dorm was built for women, so it had no urinals, and the stall partitions stopped 5 cm short of the floor. You can guess the rest.

answer-503238858.title: Where can I download recordings of high-frequency noise?

answer-502433194.title: What’s it like to date someone with a PhD?
answer-502433194.summary: Talking about research every day is compulsory. Because I’m a PhD too.

answer-502129146.title: What’s the most memorable move you’ve pulled or witnessed on a plane?
answer-502129146.summary: The German woman next to me wanted a five-letter lip tattoo and asked for ideas. My first thought was bitch; I said queen.

zhihu-45523729.title: Get in, and Go
zhihu-45523729.summary: The story takes place in July 1998: two young men from Shandong, one 21 and one 22, leave home for Beijing to find work. In 1998 I was ten, in third grade at a primary school in a county town in Northeast China, and had only once been far from home, to the provincial capital. Lately I’ve been hooked on Huang Bo’s films. I love how his performances look like no acting at all, as if he were simply being himself, when in fact the acting is off the charts: it hits you right in the heart and makes you think. A while ago I watched Cow, the film that won him the Golden Horse for best actor, and he fully deserved it. Get in, and Go was the first film of his career; it’s rough around the edges but still good, and deserves more…

answer-329981205.title: How can you get better at understanding speech at a low signal-to-noise ratio?
answer-329981205.summary: People can turn their heads to hear best. Machines such as robots and smart speakers use microphone arrays to boost the target direction and suppress the rest.

answer-329948299.title: How do the dB levels in recording and mixing differ from the decibels of everyday sounds?
answer-329948299.summary: If both are sound pressure levels, the difference lies in the reference pressure: 20 µPa for everyday sounds, the maximum of the signal for the levels that top out at 0 dB.

answer-325659908.title: Why do loudspeakers of different sizes sound different at the same volume, even setting timbre aside?
answer-325659908.summary: Low frequencies have long wavelengths and need a large diaphragm to move enough air. Small speakers have a poor low-frequency response, and that distortion is what you hear.

answer-325656939.title: What skill did you work hard to learn, only to find it was almost useless?
answer-325656939.summary: Shooting marbles. As a kid, nobody for hundreds of meters dared play me. I even made a few yuan selling my winnings.

answer-303909493.title: How do you estimate sparsity in compressed sensing?
answer-303909493.summary: Mainly read the papers by Candès and David Tao.

answer-295018157.title: Does a spectrum have any notion of time?

answer-294334067.title: Why do so many people, like, mix English words into their Chinese?

douban-note-859280264.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 13

douban-note-859262786.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 12
douban-note-859262786.summary: The five-day mahjong festival winds down. A photo trip through rime-covered countryside to a spring that never freezes, and the discovery that I feel more of a generation with my teenage nephew than with my cousin’s wife, only four years my senior.

douban-note-859226937.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 10: New Year’s Eve
douban-note-859226937.summary: Three minutes before my zodiac year begins: memories of the last one in 2012, dumplings on the sofa in front of the Spring Festival Gala, and a cigarette walk through the firecracker smoke.

douban-note-859206831.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 9
douban-note-859206831.summary: Past the halfway mark: the last bath of the Year of the Rabbit, barbecue and childhood memories, my parents’ growing fondness for drink, and another long day of mahjong at Second Aunt’s.

douban-note-859206571.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 7
douban-note-859206571.summary: The hometown interrogation at the corner shop, a welcome-home dinner where the cigarettes keep coming, and a toast that I botch completely.

douban-note-859131187.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 6
douban-note-859131187.summary: Another day of eating and loafing: stocking up on Northeastern mushrooms and pine nuts, pickled-cabbage dumplings, overpriced pajamas, and shop assistants who will not leave you alone.

douban-note-859101513.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 5
douban-note-859101513.summary: The first day of spring: a full hair salon, a brawl at the supermarket scales, an old man pocketing nuts, and a game of pool with a nephew who quit school and found his way through billiards.

douban-note-859072987.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 3

douban-note-859072605.title: Home for Chinese New Year in Northeast China, day 4
